# CI input ownership

The workflow files select their own inputs before GitHub allocates runners. Pull requests run once per head; pushes run only on `main`, providing post-merge validation without a second suite on each feature-branch push. Manual dispatch remains available for an explicit full run of one workflow. Job IDs and matrix-generated check names are unchanged.

| Workflow | Inputs and responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `check.yml` | Strict checks, unit tests, package/standalone behavior, generation, Git/isolation and Pi resource acceptance. All TypeScript and verification/build scripts belong here. |
| `lsp.yml` | Native language-server acceptance imports `code-intelligence/` and `config.ts`; changes to unrelated runtime or unit-test files do not start it. |
| `beads.yml` | Native Beads authority and runtime acceptance. The runtime fixture launches the full Studio CLI/extension, so production modules, vendored clients and packaged resources remain inputs even when they are not Beads-specific. Unrelated unit or LSP-only acceptance changes do not start this workflow. |

Package/lock changes and the routing contract are shared inputs. Every workflow selects changes to itself; the strict workflow also validates workflow-definition changes. New dependencies must be reflected in the consuming workflow's `paths`, with a routing regression demonstrating the dependency. Production entrypoints remain at their existing paths; `source-files.json` is an export boundary, not a second CI ownership registry.

Run `bun scripts/ci-selection.ts PATH...` to inspect applicable workflows and their exact Octo check names. For an existing PR pass the current target branch, for example `bun scripts/ci-selection.ts --base origin/main --head HEAD`; revision mode compares the PR merge base to the head. For push inspection pass `--event push --base BEFORE --head AFTER`. If the target branch changed CI definitions or the selection helper that the PR has not incorporated, the command requires syncing those definitions before deriving check policy; unrelated target-branch changes do not require a rebase. Revision mode reads the actual base/head workflow definitions: deleted and renamed files retain both old and new input owners, while expected check names come only from workflows present at the head. Git/ref, YAML, and unsupported-filter errors fail explicitly rather than producing a no-CI result. Set Octo's expected checks from the selected workflows, rather than requiring excluded workflows to appear. This helper does not change repository or Octo policy.

GitHub's native path filters use pull-request merge-base diffs and push before/after diffs. A required workflow excluded by paths remains pending rather than reporting success, so do not configure every path-scoped native job as an unconditional required check. Large or unavailable diffs have GitHub-defined limits and fallback behavior; use manual dispatch when a complete explicit run is needed. See [GitHub's path-filter contract](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore).

`tests/ci-selection.test.ts` parses the actual workflow files and checks selected consumers, excluded documentation/unit-test edits, workflow self changes, shared changes, and real deleted/renamed revision inputs. The native-input check follows local imports and literal repository script paths used by the acceptance/CLI sources, including the Studio launcher invoked by the runtime fixture. Its removed-edge controls demonstrate that omitting an actual dependency changes the result rather than merely asserting a list count. Computed runtime inputs still require explicit ownership review.
